factProposals.value: Every critique-intake outcome (review_created, review_already_queued, comment_no_marker, comment_rejected_malformed) every finalize check (finalize_allowed, finalize_blocked with its reason code) and every Basecamp submission retrieval (retrieval_started, then retrieval_completed or retrieval_failed with its error class, under the requesting user and project id) is written as one append-only AuditEvent carrying time, actor, outcome, correlation id and the comment/message/review ids.

An approval is allowed only when a non-AI human reviewer has recorded an 'approved' decision with non-empty feedback; every blocked attempt (NO_HUMAN_REVIEW, MISSING_REVIEWER_IDENTITY, AI_CANNOT_APPROVE, NOT_APPROVED, EMPTY_FEEDBACK) is refused with 409 and recorded with the claimed reviewer id, or 'unidentified' when none is named.
Existing SQL Server tables and stored procedures must not change; the application's SQL Server access is read-only, so application state such as the audit trail is stored outside SQL Server.

Audit events hold ids, outcomes and reason codes only (no free-text field, ids capped at 128 characters), and the audit file lives under git-ignored data/audit/, so comment bodies, personal data and secrets do not reach the audit trail or the public repo.

decisions.statement: Store the audit trail as an append-only JSON Lines file (data/audit/audit_trail.jsonl) behind an AuditTrail interface, instead of the review_audit_log SQL Server table proposed in Master Spec §19.
decisions.rationale: user rule: no changes to existing SQL Server tables or procedures; a database-backed trail can implement the same interface later if one is approved

decisions.statement: An action is refused if its audit event cannot be written: 503 from POST /basecamp/comments/process and POST /reviews/finalize-check, and AuditWriteError from process_comment/run_intake.
decisions.rationale: no submission may be processed or approved without a record

decisions.statement: The audit trail is a required argument of critique intake, not optional.
decisions.rationale: makes 'processed without logging' impossible for any caller rather than a convention

decisions.statement: A Basecamp retrieval records retrieval_started before any API call and retrieval_completed before returning data; if either cannot be written no data is returned, while a failure to record retrieval_failed never hides the original Basecamp error.
decisions.rationale: retrieval is read-only and safe to re-run, so refusing is cheap; the Basecamp error is the real cause and must stay visible

limitations.statement: The review queue and the audit trail are not written in one transaction: if the audit write fails right after a review item is created, the item stays and a re-run records it as review_already_queued rather than review_created.
The audit file's write lock is per process; several server worker processes rely on the operating system's append mode to keep each line intact.
AI/system approvers are detected with a static denylist of ids until reviewer authentication exists.
